macro.regime: A hot October CPI print and unusually blunt hawkish Fedspeak (Waller, Logan) pulled December hike odds to 100% and pushed real yields/USD higher, hitting precious metals, miners and crypto hard while index-level equities held up on mega-cap concentration even as breadth deteriorated underneath -- a genuine, broad-based repricing of the Fed path rather than a single-sector story, with Hormuz still unresolved and a fresh Nvidia governance scandal adding idiosyncratic risk into its Nov 17 print
macro.narrative: As of Tuesday Nov 10 US close, the week's cleanest macro catalyst landed hot: October CPI came in above consensus on both core (+0.3% m/m vs +0.2% expected) and headline (+0.4% vs +0.3%), with y/y readings of 2.6% core and 3.7% headline. The market reaction was immediate and hawkish -- CME-implied odds of a December hike jumped to 100% (from 84% the day before), with a 50bp move now priced at roughly 10-11% versus ~1% previously, after Fed Governor Waller said he could back a hike and possibly a larger one if core ran hot (it did), and Dallas Fed's Logan said at least two more hikes are needed. The 10Y yield jumped roughly 10bp toward 5% and the dollar strengthened (DXY +0.6% to ~102.26). Equity indices absorbed this with only a modest pullback (S&P -0.38%, Nasdaq -0.74%, VIX little-changed at 19.46) after Monday's huge semis-led rally, but breadth told a rougher story: NYSE decliners outpaced advancers roughly 2.3-2.5 to 1 (versus ~81% advancing Monday), and the net new-highs-minus-lows reading on both the S&P and Nasdaq deteriorated sharply -- the index-level calm is concentrated in a handful of large names, not broad participation. Precious metals bore the brunt of the real-yield move: gold fell 2.7% and silver 3.4%, but the miners -- which carry direct operating leverage to the metal price -- fell much harder (GDX -5.4%, SILJ -5.7 to -6.4%, SLVP -5.5%, NEM -4.2%, Barrick -2.2%, Pan American -5.8%, First Majestic -5.9%, Hecla -7.3%). Importantly, the physical market did not confirm a thesis break: COMEX registered silver inventory continued draining (now ~103.65 Moz, down ~48% from the Sept-2025 record) and stayed in backwardation, while global silver ETF holdings actually rose to their highest since March even as the futures price corrected -- consistent with a leveraged positioning flush on the rate repricing rather than a change in physical tightness. A second major idiosyncratic risk escalated: Nvidia's board confirmed its independent investigation concerns CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair with a woman US intelligence believes was feeding information to Beijing, and three House committee chairs have summoned Huang for a closed-door briefing on Nov 18 -- the day after Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings; NVDA is down more than 10% since Monday even as the rest of the chip complex (AMD, Broadcom) held up better. In Asia, China's October trade surplus narrowed to $105.3B (missing the ~$125.8B consensus) as imports (+41.6% y/y) outpaced exports (+35.2% y/y), but semiconductor export value surged 137.1% y/y and the Hang Seng/Hang Seng Tech indices still rallied (+0.44%/+1.08%) on the read-through to the AI-supply-chain story; China's M2/new-loans release has moved to Nov 13, not today as previously flagged. The Strait of Hormuz remains genuinely unresolved: a Qatar-brokered proposal (an $8B unfreeze of Iranian funds and a phased blockade lift for a reopened strait) is under White House review and Trump called the war 'effectively over' militarily, but Secretary Rubio called the proposal unrealistic and neither government has confirmed terms -- the war-risk premium in energy and the safe-haven case for gold/silver should not be unwound on hope alone. Crypto, which had looked briefly decoupled from the broader risk tone, fell in lockstep with the hawkish repricing (BTC near a 3-month low around $73,874) as spot BTC/ETH ETFs logged roughly $1.5B of net outflows since Nov 2, removing a key marginal buyer.
